content:
alex: quick thread - i've been digging into backpressure for the continuous batcher. we keep conflating 'latency SLO backpressure' and 'memory/cache pressure' into one signal. want to split taxonomy and decide where admission should react.

maria: agreed. two separate control planes make sense: one that protects latency SLOs (fast path) and one that protects resource stability (slow path).

sam: proposed primitives: token-credit admission for latency (soft throttle) + memory-watermark admission for cache/backpressure (hard trim/reject). token credits let us smooth bursts without immediate eviction.

katie: how would token-credit work for multi-tenant? do we allocate per-tenant credits or global pool with weights? fairness and runaway tenants are the worry.

sam: per-tenant weight + global reclaim. sketch: each tenant t has credits C_t that refill at rate r_t. enqueue consumes cost = f(request_size, seq_len). when C_t<cost, we either queue in a low-priority lane or apply early-preempt.

```text
// simplified
cost = tokens(req)
if credits[t] >= cost:
  accept_fast_lane()
else:
  accept_slow_lane_or_reject()
```

jordan: for memory/cache pressure we can't just rely on credits. cache GC / kvcache eviction must be coordinated with admission. suggest memory-watermarks: warn (70%), shed-batches-that-increase-kv-pressure (85%), emergency-reject (95%).

maria: that implies admission needs a cost model that estimates downstream kvcache delta for a batch. not trivial because prefix reuse affects whether a request will touch KV. we can approximate using per-route hit-rate heuristics.

katie: ops question: when we shed, do we prefer dropping requests from the back of the queue or drop entire low-priority lanes? dropping across lanes affects fairness. maybe prefer lane-local tail-drop with debt accounting so tenant gets credit recharge slower.

alex: tradeoffs: tail-drop is simple and preserves high-priority SLOs but can starve low-priority tenants. lane-drop with debt keeps isolation but increases p99 for those tenants. both options need telemetry to prove strategies.

sam: another idea: adaptive micro-shaping. reduce max-window-size dynamically for tenants when memory watermark grows. smaller windows => less KV pressure per batch but higher per-token overhead. adjustable knob.

jordan: note re: preemption: if we preempt a request that's already generated partial KV writes (or primed cache), replay/consistency becomes messy. prefer marking preempted requests as "evicted" and not allow partial side-effects until execution starts. need to audit our side-effect model.

maria: monitoring surface: per-tenant credits, refill rate, queue-depth by lane, memory-watermark, kvcache-hit-prob estimate, eviction-count. also a per-tenant SLA impact score computed from recent requeues/drops.

katie: must expose control plane flags: per-tenant weight, slow-lane window cap, eviction-priority. ops should be able to opt a tenant into conservative mode.

ops-bot: deploy: feature/credit-admission toggled in staging (flag: admission.credit_mode=true) at 2026-03-21T09:10Z :rocket:

alex: implementation plan (small):
- add credit accounting layer in admission (opt-in route flag)
- expose watermarks + reactive window cap in runtime config
- implement lane-local tail-drop + debt accounting (for fairness)
- simulation harness to run mixed-tenant workloads and measure p50/p95/p99 and memory pressure curves

sam: testers: produce scenarios with high-KV-fingerprint reuse (low kvcost) vs random input (high kvcost) to validate heuristics.

jordan: question for reviewers: do we prefer early-reject (fail-fast) or queue-then-reject? failing fast surfaces backpressure to callers (maybe better) but increases app-layer retry churn. queue-then-reject hides instability but increases headroom risk.

maria: my vote: fail-fast for public API with retry guidance + queue-then-reject for controlled internal tenants. make it configurable per-tenant.

katie: agree. add documentation to SLO playbook explaining expected caller behavior on 429 vs queue delay.

alex: ok i'll draft a short RFC: taxonomy + primitives (credits, watermarks, lane caps, debt accounting) + experiment plan. will include simulator config. ping if you want to add specific metrics to the telemetry table.

jordan: i'll add the eviction and preemption audit checklist to the RFC.

maria: thanks. small follow-up: consider a cheap estimator we can run at enqueue to predict KV delta (count unique prefix tokens or use recent route hit-rate). small model could be crucial.

sam: noted. i'll prototype a sliding-window estimator.

alex: nice thread. short action items: sam + katie prototype credits + debt, jordan + maria spec watermarks and audit, i'll write the RFC.

katie: :thumbsup:
